Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

listener noun

also listeners, hearer, the audience (those listening), a good listener

classical

Cic. Or. 24; Brut. 191 (Lewis & Short)

audītor, audītōris m.

noun, third declension

a hearer, a listener

One who hears a speech, a reading, a story; also, very often, a teacher’s pupil (Theophrastī audītor, Cic. Fin. 5.54). For a woman, quae audit.

Other words

  • quī audiunt — those who listen, the listeners

    phrase: a relative clause · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.17; Sest. 44 (Lewis & Short, s.v. audītor)

    Cicero often says it so, rather than audītōrēs (Lewis & Short).

  • auscultātor, auscultātōris m. — a listener

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Part. 10 (Lewis & Short)

    Once in Cicero; from auscultāre, to listen closely, and also to obey.

Examples

  • Attentē audītis: audītōrēs estis optimī.

    You’re listening carefully: you’re the best listeners.composed

See also hear, listen carefully, student.

SourcesLewis & Short: auditor · Lewis & Short: auscultator
